title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) Service Extension for Delivery Status Notifications (DSNs)
summary: Defines an extension to SMTP that lets a client request Delivery Status Notifications. The client can say when notifications should be generated, whether the original content should be returned, and attach extra information so the sender can identify which recipient and transaction a notice refers to.

eli5.summary: When you send a letter you can ask for a receipt. This lets email senders ask the mail system to send back a report on whether delivery worked.

questions: how to request a dsn in smtp
what does notify=never mean in smtp
subtitle: How an email sender can ask the mail system for a receipt, and say exactly when and how much to report back.

tldr.problem: Traditional SMTP bounce messages were often too thin to tell which host or which recipient had a problem, and had no standard format for exchange with other mail systems.
tldr.mechanism: An SMTP extension named DSN adds NOTIFY and ORCPT options to the RCPT command and RET and ENVID options to the MAIL command, so the sender can control when a Delivery Status Notification is generated and what it carries.
tldr.outcome: The RFC obsoletes RFC 1891 and has since been updated by RFC 3798, RFC 3885, RFC 5337, RFC 6533 and RFC 8098. Its status is Draft Standard.

today: RFC 3461 obsoletes RFC 1891 and, per the metadata, is a Draft Standard that has been updated by RFC 3798, RFC 3885, RFC 5337, RFC 6533 and RFC 8098. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Why Bounce Messages Were Not Enough
sections.content:
SMTP requires a server to notify the sender when it decides a message cannot be delivered to one or more recipients. Traditionally that notice is an ordinary Internet mail message, sent to the envelope sender address (the argument of the SMTP MAIL command), with an explanation of the error and at least the headers of the failed message.

Experience with large mailing lists showed that such messages are often not enough to diagnose problems, or even to tell at which host or for which recipients the problem occurred. There was also no standard notification format, which made it hard to swap notifications with other message handling systems.

The RFC lists what a good Delivery Status Notification (DSN) service needs. It should be reliable (a request is either honored at final delivery or answered with a statement that it cannot be), give an unambiguous success or failure answer, be stable (a failed attempt to deliver a DSN never causes another DSN), keep enough information to identify the transaction and the recipient even through forwarding and gatewaying, and work with non-SMTP mail systems.
sections.eli5: Imagine a lost parcel where the note only says 'problem'. You would want to know which parcel and where it got stuck. This RFC makes the mail system say so clearly.

sections.title: Announcing the DSN Extension
sections.content:
The extension is named "Delivery Status Notification" and its EHLO keyword is DSN, which takes no parameters. A client starts a session with EHLO. If the server answers with code 250 and the response includes the DSN keyword, the extension is supported.

The extension adds no new SMTP verbs. It adds two optional parameters to RCPT (NOTIFY and ORCPT) and two to MAIL (RET and ENVID).

Normally a 2xx reply to RCPT means the server accepts responsibility for either delivering the message or telling the sender that delivery failed. A server that implements DSN lets the client change the default, which is to issue notifications only on failure. In general such a server passes DSN requests on when relaying to other servers that support the extension, and makes a best effort to honor them when handing a message to other environments.
sections.eli5: Before asking for a receipt, you first check that the post office offers receipts. The server says DSN in its greeting if it does.

sections.title: The Four Parameters
sections.content:
NOTIFY goes on RCPT and says when to generate a DSN for that recipient. Its value is either NEVER (by itself) or a comma-separated list of SUCCESS, FAILURE and DELAY. DELAY signals willingness to receive a "delayed" DSN; leaving it out asks that no delayed DSN be issued. If NOTIFY is absent, the server may treat it as either NOTIFY=FAILURE or NOTIFY=FAILURE,DELAY.

ORCPT goes on RCPT and carries the original recipient address, in the form addr-type;xtext. It matters when mail is forwarded: if a message addressed to A@B.C is forwarded to A@D.E, the RCPT names A@D.E but the original recipient stays A@B.C. At initial submission ORCPT MUST match the RCPT TO address.

RET goes on MAIL and is FULL (return the whole message in failure DSNs) or HDRS (headers only). ENVID goes on MAIL and carries an envelope identifier chosen by the sender. The mail system assigns it no meaning; it is returned in any DSN so the sender can match the notice to the transaction.

Because ENVID and ORCPT may need characters that SMTP parameter values do not allow, they are encoded as xtext: printable ASCII from ! to ~ may stand for itself, except + and =, and anything else becomes + followed by two upper-case hexadecimal digits. Before encoding, both values MUST be printable US-ASCII.

RET and ENVID MUST NOT appear more than once in a MAIL command, and NOTIFY and ORCPT MUST NOT appear more than once in a RCPT command. A server SHOULD answer repeats with 501 syntax error in parameters or arguments.
sections.eli5: It is like filling in a form on the parcel. One box says when to send a report, one holds the name on the original address, one says how much of the parcel to send back, and one is your own tracking number.

sections.title: Rules for Relaying and Delivery
sections.content:
A server that advertises DSN must follow these rules. It MUST NOT refuse a MAIL or RCPT command because a valid DSN parameter is present or absent; the reply must be the same as without them. Invalid values or repeated parameters get a 501 reply.

Relaying to a server that supports DSN: ENVID and RET are copied unchanged if they were received and not added if they were not. NOTIFY is copied the same way. An ORCPT received MUST be passed on identically (even letter case must not change), and one MAY be added if there was none.

Relaying to a server without DSN: none of the four parameters may be sent, so the relaying MTA takes over the duty. If NOTIFY included SUCCESS and the server accepts the recipient, the client MUST issue a "relayed" DSN. If NOTIFY included FAILURE (or was absent) and the server returns a permanent 5xx failure, the client MUST issue a "failed" DSN. With NEVER no DSN may be issued.

Local delivery counts as done when the message is placed in the mailbox, or made available to an IMAP or POP service, not when the user reads it. A "delivered" DSN MUST be issued if NOTIFY included SUCCESS, and none otherwise. On failure, a "failed" DSN MUST be issued if NOTIFY included FAILURE or was absent, and MUST NOT be issued if NOTIFY was present without FAILURE.

A "delayed" DSN is never required. It MAY be sent when NOTIFY includes DELAY or is absent, and MUST NOT be sent when NOTIFY is present without DELAY.

A DSN MUST NOT be returned for a message whose SMTP return address was the null address <>. The MTA SHOULD instead tell the local postmaster by a means that does not itself generate a DSN.
sections.eli5: If the next post office cannot give receipts, your post office promises to write the receipt itself. And it never sends a receipt about a receipt that went missing.

sections.title: Aliases, Lists and Gateways
sections.content:
The RFC distinguishes an alias, where forwarding keeps the envelope return address, from a mailing list, where the return address is changed to the list administrator so that DSNs from list members go to the administrator rather than to the original sender.

For a mailing list, delivery to the list submission address is final delivery for the original message, and a "delivered" DSN MUST be returned if NOTIFY had SUCCESS. When the list redistributes the message, the return address is rewritten and ENVID, NOTIFY, RET and ORCPT MUST NOT be derived from the original message.

A single-recipient alias should not issue a DSN, and the parameters SHOULD be passed on. For an alias with several recipients the RFC allows three handling choices: pass nothing on and issue a "relayed" DSN if SUCCESS was asked for; pass everything to exactly one address with no DSN; or pass ENVID, RET and ORCPT to all, strip SUCCESS from NOTIFY, and issue an "expanded" DSN if SUCCESS was requested.

Treating a forwarding address like a mailing list can keep it confidential, since later failures go back to the new return address and not to the original sender.

When gatewaying into a non-SMTP environment, the MTA SHOULD hand over the notification request if that environment can honor it, and otherwise issue a "relayed" DSN when SUCCESS was requested. RET is non-binding there, though the MTA SHOULD try to honor it.
sections.eli5: If a letter goes to a club, the club's secretary becomes the person who hears about problems with members' copies. That keeps members' private addresses secret.

sections.title: What a DSN Looks Like
sections.content:
The DSN format itself is defined elsewhere (RFC 3464, using the framework of RFC 3462). This RFC adds the rules for DSNs about messages received over SMTP.

When a DSN is sent over SMTP, the sender address in MAIL MUST be the null reverse-path <>, and the recipient is copied from the MAIL command of the message being reported. RET MUST NOT be used, and NOTIFY MAY be used only with the value NEVER. This is what stops DSNs from triggering further DSNs.

A DSN is a MIME message with top-level type multipart/report and report-type delivery-status. Its first part is a human-readable explanation, the second is message/delivery-status, and the third is the original message or part of it. With RET=FULL the full message SHOULD be returned for failures, though an MTA MAY send only headers if the message is longer than some implementation-specific length. A DSN with no failures SHOULD return only headers.

In the message/delivery-status part, the ENVID value MUST appear as Original-Envelope-ID (decoded from xtext) and the ORCPT value as Original-Recipient. The Reporting-MTA, Final-Recipient, Action and Status fields MUST be supplied. When no specific status code fits, 4.0.0 (temporary failure) or 5.0.0 (permanent failure) MUST be used. The appendices define the rfc822 address type, the smtp diagnostic type and the dns MTA name type.
sections.eli5: The receipt is a small package with three parts: a note in plain words, a form with the details, and a copy of the original letter.

sections.title: Size Limits
sections.content:
A conforming MTA MUST accept at least these parameter sizes: ENVID 100 characters, NOTIFY 28 characters, ORCPT 500 characters and RET 8 characters. User agents that submit mail with SMTP SHOULD NOT generate ENVID values longer than 38 characters.

The MTA MUST also accept command lines of at least 1036 characters: 530 characters for the ORCPT and NOTIFY parameters of RCPT, plus the 512 characters that SMTP itself requires.
sections.eli5: Each box on the form has a minimum size so every post office can read what you write.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The extension does not change the fundamental nature of SMTP and so creates no new security exposures by itself. It does add complexity, and with it a greater risk of implementation errors.

The RFC notes that earlier ad-hoc delivery notification schemes sometimes caused a storm of receipts through unplanned interaction with mailing list software. Success notification here is designed so that, if properly implemented, it cannot interact with a list expander that way. Wider issues are covered in the security sections of RFC 3462 and RFC 3464.
sections.eli5: Receipts can pile up if every list member's receipt goes to the same person. The rules are built so that cannot happen.

items.label: No DSN
items.desc: No DSN is returned to the sender under any condition; must appear alone.

items.label: Delivered
items.desc: Issue a DSN on successful delivery.

items.label: Failed
items.desc: Issue a DSN on delivery failure.

items.label: Delayed
items.desc: Willing to receive a delayed DSN when delivery is held up for an unusual time.

viz.caption: SUBMISSION EXCERPT FROM THE RFC'S APPENDIX EXAMPLE

data.title: Client requests with DSN parameters
data.code:
>>> EHLO Example.ORG
<<< 250-Example.ORG
<<< 250-DSN
>>> MAIL FROM:<Alice@Example.ORG> RET=HDRS ENVID=QQ314159
>>> RCPT TO:<Bob@Example.COM> NOTIFY=SUCCESS \
    ORCPT=rfc822;Bob@Example.COM
>>> RCPT TO:<Fred@Bombs.AF.MIL> NOTIFY=NEVER
